0:
set -eu

backup_dir=/backup
keep=30
incoming="$$backup_dir/.incoming.xml"
trap 'rm -f "$$incoming"' EXIT

# --insecure matches the exporter and the firmware-check job: the
# firewall serves its own cert on the LAN address.
curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --insecure \
  --max-time 120 --retry 3 --retry-delay 10 \
  --request POST \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --user "$$OPNSENSE_API_KEY:$$OPNSENSE_API_SECRET" \
  --data "{}" \
  --output "$$incoming" \
  "https://opnsense.${SECRET_DOMAIN}/api/core/backup/download/this"

# HTTP status alone does not prove we got a config -- some OPNsense
# error paths answer 200 with a JSON body. Validate the payload, or
# the job "succeeds" while storing a 36-byte error as this month's
# only backup. This is the same failure class as a backup that looks
# like coverage and restores nothing.
if ! head -c 512 "$$incoming" | grep -q "<opnsense>"; then
  echo "FATAL: response has no <opnsense> root element. First bytes:" >&2
  head -c 512 "$$incoming" >&2
  exit 1
fi

size=$(wc -c < "$$incoming")
if [ "$$size" -lt 10000 ]; then
  echo "FATAL: config is only $$size bytes, expected well over 10k" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Only keep a copy when the config actually changed, so the directory
# reads as a change history instead of 30 identical files. config.xml
# carries a <revision> block that OPNsense rewrites on every config
# change, so the checksum moves exactly when the configuration does.
new_sum=$(sha256sum < "$$incoming" | cut -d' ' -f1)
latest=$(find "$$backup_dir" -maxdepth 1 -name 'config-*.xml' | sort | tail -n1)
if [ -n "$$latest" ] && [ "$$new_sum" = "$(sha256sum < "$$latest" | cut -d' ' -f1)" ]; then
  echo "config unchanged since $(basename "$$latest") -- verified $$size bytes, nothing written"
  exit 0
fi

# UTC in the name so lexical sort is chronological, which is what the
# prune below depends on. mv is atomic within the same filesystem, so
# a mover killed mid-write never leaves a truncated config-*.xml that
# the next run would checksum against.
target="$$backup_dir/config-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%SZ).xml"
mv "$$incoming" "$$target"
# 0600 keeps the cleartext config out of casual reach, but it is not
# the security boundary -- NFSv4 with sys auth trusts whatever uid the
# client asserts, so the export's allowed-hosts list is what actually
# protects this. It does mean an SMB session that maps to a uid other
# than 1000 cannot read these files; restore via the TrueNAS shell or
# web file browser (root ignores the mode) if that bites.
chmod 0600 "$$target"
echo "wrote $$target ($$size bytes)"

find "$$backup_dir" -maxdepth 1 -name 'config-*.xml' | sort -r | tail -n +$((keep + 1)) | while read -r old; do
  echo "pruning $$old"
  rm -f "$$old"
done

/hr/ghcr.io-bjw-s-labs-charts-immich-mic.doc:
Immich is a self-hosted photo and video backup solution.

For immich, there are multiple helm deployments:

  • immich-web
  • immich-server
  • immich-typesense
  • immich-machine-learning
  • immich-microservices (this one)

For redis and postgres, there are multiple helm charts:

  • Redis: app-template/redis, bitnami/redis
  • PostgreSQL: operator cloudnative-pg/cloudnative-pg, bitnami bitnami/postgresql
